# The step contract — 18 categories, 299 declarable fields

**Contract version 1 · status `v0-unfrozen-until-C3`.** The schema is canonical; this document is generated from it. Editing this file changes nothing.

**Legend:** † required · ~ derived, do not declare · ! extending is a RUNNER CHANGE, never a per-step invention · ⛔ banned for new steps.

> **Omission is a build failure; `"none"` is a legal value that must be written down — per field, not per category.** The schema is closed: an unknown key fails the build, which is what stops `"None"` and `"n/a"` existing as improvised strings.

## Archetype required-field profiles

`identity.archetype` is not a label — it drives which of the categories are live. A new ENRICHER cannot omit its invalidator, because its archetype makes the field required.

| Archetype | Forces |
|---|---|
| `ASSERT` | outputs = `none` · recovery = `none` · counters = `none` |
| `INGESTOR` | outputs is object |
| `LINK / MATCHER` | outputs.invalidates min 1 · counters is object |
| `ENRICHER` | outputs is object · **if staleness.scope is a predicate ⇒ outputs.invalidates min 1** |
| `MATERIALIZER / BACKFILL` | outputs is object · recovery.reset != `none` |
| `RECORDER` | outputs.publish in `direct`/`pointer` |

## Mechanic semantics (V7)

> write_discipline.class names the write MECHANIC ONLY. Guardedness lives in `guard`, scope in `scope`, retraction in `retract`. Three of the 13 names still read as fused because the names are ported and frozen — read them as mechanics:

| Class value | Read it as |
|---|---|
| `guarded_upsert` | MECHANIC: keyed upsert (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE). The word 'guarded' is historical — whether it is guarded is read from `guard`, never from this name. |
| `insert_only_no_retraction` | MECHANIC: insert-only (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING). Whether it retracts is read from `retract`; the ban is the rule no_retraction, not this name. |
| `set_based_scoped` | MECHANIC: set-based UPDATE. Whether it is scoped is read from `scope`, not from this name. |
| `set_based_unscoped` | MECHANIC: set-based UPDATE — the same mechanic as set_based_scoped. Retained as a distinct value only so existing descriptors keep their ported label; the ban is the rule unscoped_set_based, evaluated over `scope`. |

## ⛔ Banned for new steps

Grandfathered, never legal for a new step: an existing step must be able to declare its truth.

| Field | Banned values |
|---|---|
| `outputs.writes[].replay` | `append_unsafe` |
| `outputs.writes[].write_discipline.guard` | `none` |
| `execution.criticality` | `best_effort` |

**Rules, not fused class identities (V7).** A ban evaluated over the decoupled axes says what is actually wrong; a ban carried inside a class name says only what the label was.

| Rule | Banned when | Was | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `no_retraction` | write_discipline.class is an insert-only mechanic AND retract == "none" | class D (insert_only_no_retraction) as a fused identity | A W3 retraction breach. Under V7 the ban is a predicate over the mechanic and the retraction axis, so a step that inserts only but DOES retract elsewhere is no longer mislabelled as breaching. |
| `unscoped_set_based` | write_discipline.class is a set-based mechanic AND write_discipline.scope == "none" | class H (set_based_unscoped) as a fused identity | An unscoped set-based UPDATE rewrites rows it never examined. Scope is now its own declared axis, so the ban is evaluable instead of being carried inside a class name. |
| `unguarded_write` | write_discipline.guard == "none" | not previously expressible at all — the source of GAP-1 and GAP-2 | V7 decoupling: guardedness left the class name and became the `guard` axis, so an unguarded write is now DECLARABLE (with a why) rather than unlabellable. Grandfathered only — banned for new steps. |

## ⚠️ Menu completeness — RESOLVED-BY-V7 — per-file verification still owed

*The 5 known evidence-base §3f mislabels were re-derived FROM THE SQL, not from the ported labels, so the 13-class enum is not authored against known-bad data.* `[MEASURED 2026-08-24 (S1, ruling R5); gaps closed by operator ruling V7 the same day]`

| Step | Correction |
|---|---|
| `load_heritage` | A -> B. :602 is a literal `DELETE FROM <t> WHERE source_id <> ALL($1::BIGINT[])` departure delete against its own table, behind an empty-set guard (:598). The base's Del=0 is factually wrong. |
| `load_zoning` | A -> B (x11 layer tables). The departure delete at :526-528 is a NOT EXISTS anti-join against a keys-only TEMP table. The suspected class C is REFUTED: the temp table holds keys only and is never the source of an INSERT...SELECT, so it is a mechanic of B, not a full replace. |
| `load_neighbourhoods` | A -> A + 6 INEXPRESSIBLE. Confirmed: exactly 2 IS DISTINCT FROM in the whole file (:153, :154), both in the upsert. The 6 profile UPDATEs (:473, :486, :506, :543, :563, :603) have NO guard at all. Also VACUUM ANALYZE at :680 -> execution.maintenance. |
| `link_wsib` | K -> E + G. Three targets: wsib_registry link-columns are E (WHERE linked_entity_id IS NULL), entities.is_wsib_registered is G (guarded + scoped by match_confidence), entities contact columns are E in blank-or-null form. There is no derived_recompute anywhere in the file; K is simply absent. |
| `refresh_snapshot` | M -> INEXPRESSIBLE. :535 is `ON CONFLICT (snapshot_date) DO UPDATE SET ... created_at=NOW()` with no change guard — a same-day re-run overwrites all columns of that day's row in place. It is not append-only. |

| Gap | Pattern | Sites | Why no value fitted | Now declarable as | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **GAP-1** | unguarded set-based UPDATE — no IS DISTINCT FROM at all | `load-neighbourhoods.js:473,486,506,543,563,603` | Under the FUSED enum: G required guard AND scope; H required a guard WITHOUT scope; E required an IS NULL predicate; I required a temp table; J required multi-pass + defer; K did not cover source-loaded non-derived columns (avg/median household income, period_of_construction). Every available value would have recorded a guard the SQL does not contain. | class: set_based_scoped (MECHANIC) + guard: "none" (+guard_why) + scope: the profile-refresh predicate, or scope: "none" (+why) where the refresh genuinely spans the table. | EXPRESSIBLE — the per-site declaration is owed at the INGESTOR pilot's PH-0. |
| **GAP-2** | unguarded keyed upsert — ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE with no change guard | `refresh-snapshot.js:535` | Under the FUSED enum: A meant GUARDED upsert; D covered DO NOTHING; M meant append-only INSERT. All three misstated an in-place same-day overwrite. | class: guarded_upsert (MECHANIC: keyed upsert) + guard: "none" (+guard_why) + scope: "snapshot_date = CURRENT_DATE". | EXPRESSIBLE — the declaration is owed at the RECORDER pilot's PH-0. |

**Root cause:** The enum FUSED the write mechanic with the change guard, so every write that lacked a guard fell off the menu.

**Resolution:** CLOSED BY OPERATOR RULING V7 (2026-08-24): mechanic, guard, scope and retraction are four declared axes; `guard: none` makes an unguarded write DECLARABLE (with a why) instead of unlabellable, and the D/H bans became validator rules over the axes. No enum value was invented. ⚠️ WHAT IS NOT CLOSED: the seven sites above are expressible, not yet declared — each owning pilot must verify its own writes at PH-0 and produce the declaration. The contract is still v0 and freezes at C3.

- Class B is written as the literal `DELETE ... WHERE key <> ALL($1)`, but load-zoning expresses the identical departure delete as a NOT EXISTS anti-join. B must be read BY INTENT, not by literal syntax, or load_zoning becomes a third gap.
- Classes C and I both presuppose a temp table used for full-replace / update-from; load-zoning uses one purely to scope a delete. Harmless under the per-target rule only if that rule is stated explicitly: an ON COMMIT DROP scratch table is not a write target.

## Rulings encoded

| # | Ruling |
|---|---|
| **V1** | identity.archetype uses FULL WORDS; the ING|MAT|... forms are display shorthand only and are not legal values. |
| **V2** | identity.lock is unique across manifest UNION one-time/ UNION backfill/ — the wider universe, not the generated registry alone. Cross-file uniqueness is a validator-side check (S2); JSON Schema cannot express it. |
| **V3** | guards.schema_drift is none|propagate|pause. 'warn' is DROPPED — a drift response is an action; warn-ness belongs to the orthogonal severity/blocking axes. |
| **V4** | outputs.writes[].replay keeps append_unsafe in the enum but BANNED FOR NEW STEPS via x-banned-for-new, so an existing step can still declare its truth. |
| **V5** | staleness.pending is DISSOLVED into three axes: scope (which rows) / trigger (what makes the step eligible) / mode_select (what the trigger chooses), plus fingerprint_inputs. |
| **V6** | guards.empty_source is the typed form <table> | [<table>,...] | none — AS AMENDED 2026-08-24. The original ruling typed the scalar form only; the array form is a ratified amendment recorded in Spec 122's V-table, needed because a step may guard on more than one source table (enrich_heritage guards on heritage_properties AND heritage_districts, Spec 120 §3.3). Recorded as an amendment rather than restated silently. |
| **R6-acquisition** | NOT a category. Absorbed as staleness.trigger[].position (the acquisition lifecycle position) + inputs.reads.externals[].cache. |
| **R6-maintenance** | NOT a category. Absorbed as execution.maintenance — declares targets and CONSTRAINS txn_scope (VACUUM cannot run inside a transaction). |
| **R6-terminals** | A NEW CATEGORY (the 18th). Declared exit paths, each with its records_meta shape. Retires the hand-written per-terminal 'PASS'. |
| **R6-plan_shape** | NOT a category. A checks[].kind value. |
| **R6-source_key_policy** | NOT a category. A per-target field: outputs.writes[].source_key_policy. |
| **R6-on_missing** | guards.requires[].on_missing is fail|degrade; degrade requires why AND algorithm, because a degraded branch makes outputs.columns a fiction. |
| **V7** | DECOUPLE MECHANIC FROM GUARD (operator ruling, 2026-08-24, closing the S1 menu-completeness gap). write_discipline.class names the write MECHANIC only; guardedness is `guard` (is_distinct_from|none, none requires a why and is grandfathered-only), scope is `scope`, retraction is `retract`. The D and H bans are restated as VALIDATOR RULES over those axes — banned-for-new = (insert-only mechanic AND retract:none) and (set-based mechanic AND scope:none) — not as fused class identities. |
| **R6-schema_drift-conditional** | guards.schema_drift may be a SCALAR or a CONDITIONAL PER-LAYER ARRAY (the load-zoning.js:405-407 shape: base layers FAIL/pause, non-base WARN/propagate). A scalar cannot express it. |

## Refuted — must not be re-asserted

- `checks[].severity` — PASS is IMPOSSIBLE as a declared severity — it is a runtime outcome, never a declarable escalation target (Spec 122 §12.5). The declarable menu is INFO|WARN|FAIL.
- `identity.gate_exempt` — The claim 'declaring archetype retires run-chain.js:544-550' is REFUTED — isInfraStep spans four archetypes plus name-specific exceptions. gate_exempt is the explicit field the retirement needs.
- `counters-null-for-ASSERT` — 'An ASSERT emits counters: null' is REFUTED AS DESCRIPTION (0 of 5 ASSERTs do today). It is retained as a NORMATIVE requirement per §1.10's required-field profile: the descriptor must declare counters: "none".
